Variants.Content: The Iron Islands have barren land and dangerous reefs. The islanders have long relied on fishing, hunting, salt, ships, trade and plunder to survive. The price of iron advocates wealth obtained by force, while the price of gold refers to the income gained from purchase; the two are not all part of the daily life of the islanders, such as repairing ships, drying fish, storing grain, etcRaising sheep and waiting for the weather also constitute real daily life. The ancient paths of the Ironborn give glory to warriors, and the belief in the Drowned God gives meaning to death. However, the salt concubine system and the tradition of plunder also leave scars of violence and the captives. Outsiders see the Ironborn as just pirates, while the islanders would say that they were people who were forced to survive by the sea first.
